findings: Root cause is confirmed in code: loadConfig performs a shallow merge `{...base, ...override}`, so any key present in production.env unconditionally wins over base.env. CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=0 in production.env therefore overrides the documented 300s value in every production request — this is the direct, sole cause of caching being ineffective, and configLoader.ts itself is working exactly as designed (the bug is stale data, not merge logic).

The override's origin is a 'temporary debug: disable cache to reproduce issue #412' commit from 8 months ago that was never reverted. This is a classic stale-debug-flag defect: a change meant to be transient was left in a permanent, always-loaded production config file with no expiry, no linked follow-up/cleanup task, and no marker distinguishing it from a permanent setting.

The debug CACHE_TTL_SECONDS=0 change was committed together with an unrelated, intentional DB_POOL_SIZE=20→50 change in the same commit. This coupling means a naive fix (git revert of that commit) would also undo the legitimate pool-size increase — the fix must surgically remove only the CACHE_TTL_SECONDS line, not revert the commit wholesale.

Internal documentation states a 300-second TTL and was never updated to reflect the per-environment override, so anyone consulting the docs (rather than reading production.env directly) would reasonably but incorrectly believe caching was active in production — a docs/config drift with no reconciliation process.

There is no automated check (test or CI assertion) that verifies the effective/merged production config matches the documented values, which is why a one-line debug override could silently diverge from spec for 8 months without detection.

Because DB_POOL_SIZE was raised in the same commit that disabled caching, it may have been sized (deliberately or coincidentally) for a no-cache, all-requests-hit-DB load profile; re-enabling the cache changes the DB load pattern, so DB_POOL_SIZE=50 should be re-validated rather than assumed still correct once the cache fix ships.
